- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–30% for near-term (1–7d) horizon.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 10–25% for short-term (1–7d) to capture reversal.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., 3–5d high) — cap forecast at 2x recent peak for 1–3d horizon to avoid overshoot.
- For 10+ day horizons, model underestimates mean reversion; add 5–15% buffer to forecast based on recent volatility.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.33, 1.00, -0.33), model tends to misalign with sentiment direction — adjust forecast to match sentiment trend direction.
- When sentiment is flat (0.00–0.33) for 3+ consecutive days, model often fails to recognize mean reversion — apply downward bias of 5–10% for 7–14d horizon.
